A-17 Ticket-checker (gate staff) accounts

Bangla name: টিকিট-চেকার (গেট স্টাফ) অ্যাকাউন্ট

← 10 · Admin portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Ticket-checker accounts. Gate staff sign in to the checker app with an account in the TicketChecker Cognito pool. Admins create and manage these accounts here: create, rename, disable, enable, reset password, delete, search. How the Cognito user, its attributes and the SMS with the password are produced is described once in X-05; the checker's login is X-12; assigning checkers to gates is A-18.

2. Trigger and actor

Staff in the global menu (Users → Ticket Checkers, /ticket-checker, LimitedMenuGuard: program must be 0). TicketCheckerController allows roles admin, event_manager, ticket_manager, ticket_operator (BCBPersonnel); search is limited to admin and event_manager.

3. Business flow

  1. List checkers (name, phone, status). 2. Create with name and phone: the account exists at once and the new checker receives an SMS with the user name and a generated password. 3. Edit the name. 4. Disable or enable the account (disabled staff cannot sign in). 5. Set password generates a new password and sends it by SMS. 6. Delete the account.

4. Technical flow

  1. [HTTP + user token] List GET /admin/api/v1/ticket-checker; one GET .../ticket-checker/{id}; search GET .../ticket-checker/search?name= (used when assigning gates, A-18) and search-by-userid?sub=.
  2. Create POST .../ticket-checker with { "name", "phone" } → TicketCheckerManager.CreateUserAsync → TicketCheckerUserProvider.CreateUserAsync: AdminCreateUser in the TicketChecker pool (username = phone, e-mail attribute built from the phone, custom:role = TicketChecker), a generated password, then the credentials SMS through the notification service ([HTTP, static key], X-22). Details: X-05.
  3. Update PUT .../ticket-checker/{id} with { userId, name }: the body's userId is used, not the path id; only the name is changed.
  4. POST .../ticket-checker/disable/{id}, enable/{id}; POST .../ticket-checker/set-password?userId=; DELETE .../ticket-checker/{id}; PUT .../ticket-checker/change-password (checker changes their own password with an access token).
  5. The gate list of one checker: GET /admin/api/v1/ticket-checker-gate/user/{userId} , and per gate PUT .../ticket-checker-gate/update-download-status/{userId}/{gateId}/{status}, DELETE .../ticket-checker-gate/remove-user/{id} (A-18).

Primary sample, POST /admin/api/v1/ticket-checker:

{ "name": "Rahim Uddin", "phone": "+8801700000099" }

Response TicketCheckerUserResponse: userId, name, email, phone, role, currentStatus, isActive, isPhoneNumberVerified. Note the response field isPhoneNumberVerified is false because of a typo in the provider (see X-05).

7. Data and side effects

Cognito user in the TicketChecker pool; SMS with the password; activity log entries are written for database tables only, not for Cognito changes made here (unlike admin users, A-25).

9. Handover notes

  1. Passwords travel by SMS in clear text and are generated with System.Random (X-05, X-22).
  2. Any of four staff roles can create and delete checker accounts, including ticket_operator (BCBPersonnel), although the portal shows the Ticket Checkers menu in the global menu only to a subset (X-17).
  3. PUT .../{id} ignores the path id and trusts userId in the body, so a caller can rename a different account than the URL says.
  4. If the SMS fails, the account still exists with a password nobody has (the call order is create user, set password, send SMS); use Set password to resend (X-22 note 4).
  5. Deleting a checker does not remove gate assignments in TicketCheckerGateUsers (the delete targets Cognito); remove the assignment first in A-18 [UNCONFIRMED: Q-26].
  6. The checker's own change-password takes the access token in the request body, not the Authorization header.

11. Developer test guide

Local testability: Partial. Cognito is Floci; the SMS call fails because the notification endpoint is dummy (X-22), so creation returns an error after the Cognito user is created.
